transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-04 09:00 PDT | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Fernandez (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (Polaris - Head of Search), Tom Nguyen (Polaris - ML Eng), Raj Patel (Polaris - CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm maya from redwood, i'll run quick intro then hand over to luis for the technical stuff.
[00:12] Aisha: hi, thanks uh for doing this. quick context - we're reworking our search stack across docs + product content, want to add semantic rerank and evaluate embeddings providers.
[00:20] Raj: timeline is quarter end, security is a hard req, we need SOC2 + VPC options.
[00:27] Maya: perfect, that's in scope. quick question - are you currently using any vector DB?
[00:32] Tom: we're on Milvus for ANN, elastic for BM25, and a small pinecone POC in prod for some services. mixing is messy.
[00:40] Luis: got it. so hybrid search today: BM25 for recall then ANN for rerank? how many queries per second roughly?
[00:48] Aisha: steady 150-200 qps, peak can hit 500 during campaigns, median doc size ~2k tokens, re-rank topK 50.
[00:57] Luis: okay that helps. what embedding dim are you using now?
[01:02] Tom: we tried 1536 for some models, but also test 768 to save cost. 1536 gave better quality on our eval sets.
[01:10] Maya: realistically the tradeoff is cost/latency vs quality. Redwood can serve either hosted or dedicated; dedicated gives predictable throughput esp for spikes.
[01:18] Raj: can Dedicated sit in our VPC? we need private networking and kms.
[01:22] Luis: yes, our Private and Dedicated offerings support customer VPC peering and bring-your-own KMS/HSM. there are options for on-prem too if you need air-gap.
[01:30] Aisha: great. what's the integration surface with Milvus/Pinecone? we don't want to rip and replace the whole stack.
[01:35] Luis: we typically integrate at two points - either index embeddings externally (push embeddings from your pipeline into Milvus) and call Redwood for embedding generation only, or Redwood can host both embeddings + ANN via managed index connectors. for milvus you can keep your cluster; we provide exporter scripts and a small connector that writes vectors with metadata.
[01:48] Tom: any latency hit if embeddings are generated in Hosted mode vs Dedicated?
[01:52] Luis: Hosted adds network round trips to our API, usually sub 50-70ms per embedding call for small batches; Dedicated in your region with colocated GPUs can drop that to 10-20ms per vector generation depending on batch size and GPU type. overall rerank latency includes embed time + ANN search + re-ranker model if you run one.
[02:07] Aisha: our SLO is p95 < 250ms for the full query path, including rerank. possible?
[02:12] Luis: yes but it depends on rerank model size and whether you run on the same instance. for a lightweight cross-encoder (hundreds of millions params) Dedicated can meet that easily if you pin capacity and enable KV/prefix caching and smaller topK for initial pass.
[02:25] Raj: curious about batching/caching - we've had cold start problems with KV cache misses.
[02:30] Luis: our runtime does continuous batching + KV cache retention tuned to query patterns. cold start can be mitigated by warmed instances and preloading hot prefixes; we can also provide suggestions on autoscale warmers.
[02:41] Tom: on dimensionality - if we drop to 768, what's the expected impact for rerank?
[02:45] Luis: generally 1536 yields better nearest-neighbor fidelity for diverse corpora; 768 can be fine if you combine with BM25 + a stronger reranker; that hybrid approach reduces ANN cost because BM25 narrows recall set. quantization is also an option - 16-bit/8-bit or product quantization can reduce memory and latency for ANN.
[03:05] Aisha: have you seen folks do hybrid where they generate smaller embeddings at inference and then use a heavier reranker only on top 10?
[03:12] Maya: yeah that's a common pattern - cheap embedding for recall, then cross-encoder on top-k. reduces cost while preserving quality.
[03:18] Tom: can Redwood support dynamic rerank where we fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes?
[03:22] Luis: yes we support routing policies and fallbacks - you can route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. on spike we can redirect to a lower-cost variant automatically.
[03:31] Aisha: what's the operational model for guaranteed throughput? our spikes are sudden - campaigns start with big bursts.
[03:36] Luis: Dedicated with reserved capacity and burst pools is the recommended for that pattern. you commit a baseline and allow configured burst with SLA. autoscaling also supports rapid scaling but burst pools avoid cold starts.
[03:46] Raj: how do we keep costs predictable for reranking? cost per request with cross-encoders can be high.
[03:51] Maya: two levers - reduce topK, use lighter embed dims, or run cross-encoder only on the narrowed set. Redwood Optimize suggests config combos for your workload and projects token/unit cost impact.
[04:05] Tom: onboarding - what's the pilot look like? we want a quick bench with 10k queries and our corpus.
[04:11] Luis: we can run a benchmark on Dedicated or Hosted. Typical pilot: you provide corpus + queries, we run 200 QPS steady-state with spike tests to 500 and measure p95/p99 latencies, memory, and cost estimates. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:25] Aisha: nice. about connectors - would we lose metadata fidelity when pushing vectors from our existing Milvus indexes?
[04:30] Luis: no, metadata roundtrip is preserved; we map fields and keep IDs. occasional mismatches happen due to schema differences but we provide migration helpers.
[04:39] Tom: any caveats with quantized vectors in Milvus? we've used PQ for storage.
[04:44] Luis: PQ is fine for storage; for rerank accuracy you may want IVF+PQ tuned for recall. also consider hybrid search using exact search for top small N then ANN for larger sets.
[04:55] Aisha: security - we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, egress controls.
[04:59] Luis: we have SOC2, SAML, RBAC, KMS integrations, and audit logs in Private/Dedicated. we'll share the security pack link after the call.
[05:09] Raj: if we do Private, do you still manage the control plane?
[05:12] Luis: Private offers a customer-controlled data plane with optional control plane. you can choose to self-host control plane if required. there are tradeoffs on update cadence.
[05:20] Maya: are there any blockers we should be aware of?
[05:22] Aisha: nothing major, maybe procurement timeline - legal will want the security docs before pilot.
[05:27] Maya: understood, i'll send the docs and pricing.
[05:30] Tom: one more technical - what's the recommended embedding model family? open models vs proprietary?
[05:34] Luis: for many customers we recommend 1536-dims model family for semantic tasks; if you need faster cheaper options, a 768 model with a good reranker works. Redwood also has model catalog with vetted open models; we can recommend specific checkpoints and quantization profiles.
[05:50] Aisha: ok let's recap next steps.
[05:52] Maya: recap: 1) redwood to send pricing + Dedicated pilot terms, 2) redwood to share security/SOC2 pack, 3) tom to send sample dataset, 4) schedule benchmark next week.
[06:10] Raj: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:14] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links to the benchmark sheet and connectors repo.
[06:20] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors and shorthand; speaker labels approximate. Mentioned artifacts: pricing deck (link to be shared), security pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), connectors repo (github link).
